newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UNICE wants clear EU treaty for businesses.
newsitem.headline: UNICE wants clear EU treaty for businesses.

text.p: Europe's employers called on EU leaders on Wednesday to take greater account of the needs of large and small businesses as they prepare the European Union for the future.

UNICE, the Union of Industrial and Employer's Confederations of Europe, said its president, Francois Perigot, had written to Irish Prime Minister John Bruton to express the group's concerns ahead of the informal European Council in Dublin on Saturday.
The summit has been called to give momentum to the inter-governmental conference (IGC) which is preparing for wide enlargement.
"The reshaping of Europe must bring about greater clarity and effectiveness without ever losing sight of the need to restore our competitiveness," UNICE said in a statement.
UNICE said the EU needed to draft a "specific and clear" treaty not a wish-list for the future.
"The European Union should not raise false hopes, since it will be the first loser when they prove unattainable," it said in a statement.

It said competitiveness needed to be boosted across the Union in order to create jobs, and also urged the leaders to make sure public services such as transport and telecommunications were subject to the rules of competition.
The EU treaty needed to be amended to provide for cost-benefit analyses for all new EU regulations, UNICE said.
UNICE also endorse giving the European Commission more power over trade matters.
